Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Coverage is overwhelmingly dominated by the U.S. midterm elections and their market implications, with business outlets framing the vote as a referendum on the AI-infrastructure buildout, affordability, and divided government. Layered on top is a broader 'AI trade' unwind — disappointing Big Tech reactions, Anthropic's contested IPO valuation, and Wall Street jitters over AI financing — alongside recurring threads on Middle East tensions, Saudi Aramco earnings, and a wave of European supermarket cyberattacks.

stories.headline: Wall Street braces as voters go to polls in high-stakes US midterm elections
stories.summary: FT frames the midterms as a vote that will set the trajectory for AI policy and public spending, while Axios's final forecast roundup cites election modelers giving Democrats a 95% chance of winning the House and 80% the Senate, with some models projecting their largest majority since Obama's first year.

stories.headline: AI boom hits a wall on Wall Street as spending fears spook investors
stories.summary: Fortune reports that after a brutal tech-stock selloff, OpenAI slashed its fundraising target to $20 billion from $30 billion and cut its expected valuation to $1.25 trillion from $1.4 trillion, even as Anthropic's IPO filing showed soaring revenue and positive cash flow in contrast.

stories.headline: Apple's earnings beat masked by AI anxiety and memory-chip costs
stories.summary: WSJ notes Apple remains a rare big-tech play not fully bet on the AI boom, while Fortune reports Apple beat September-quarter earnings expectations yet investors sold the stock after hours over margin pressure from a memory-chip shortage and slowing services growth.

stories.headline: Anthropic investors push back on IPO valuation
stories.summary: Institutional investors are reportedly pressuring Anthropic to price its IPO toward the lower end of a $1.5-2 trillion range after Fortune notes analysts found any valuation above roughly $1.41 trillion would require paying more than $40 for every dollar of revenue, a level reached by only 14 of over 4,000 IPOs since 1980.

stories.headline: North Korea denies role in record $6.3 billion Binance hack
stories.summary: In an unusual move, Kim Jong Un's sister issued a swift public denial of Pyongyang's involvement in the heist, even as Fortune notes the hack has been linked to an elite North Korean hacking team by the FBI.

stories.headline: Saudi Aramco profit surges despite pipeline and refinery attacks
stories.summary: State-owned Saudi Aramco posted a profit boost attributed to higher crude volumes sold and stronger prices for refined and chemical products, offering relief to the kingdom's finances even after damaging strikes on its infrastructure.

stories.headline: Supermarket freezer cyberattacks spread across Europe, Pentagon investigates U.S. link
stories.summary: A wave of disruptions at grocery stores across Europe, which officials suspect are cyberattacks, has renewed on Monday, and Fortune reports the Pentagon's criminal investigators are probing whether similar freezer failures at U.S. military commissaries in August were connected.

stories.headline: U.S. strikes Iran's Qeshm Island, reviving oil-market fears after midterms
stories.summary: The strike follows President Trump downplaying the odds of renewed war with Iran after the midterms, and Axios reports investors are watching whether a post-election 'reescalation' could spike oil prices and pressure the broader market.

Business.gaps: No current coverage was found from The Information or Puck; Business Insider blocks search and no relevant feed items were provided for it.

US politics.overview: Coverage across nearly every outlet is overwhelmingly focused on the 2026 midterm elections, with control of both the House and Senate up for grabs and Cook Political Report's final ratings showing Democrats favored in both chambers. Secondary threads include a late Supreme Court ruling rejecting a Trump DOJ bid to freeze California ballots, intensifying Trump administration legal fights over election administration, a late-breaking endorsement bombshell in Michigan's Senate race, and renewed U.S.-Iran military tension landing squarely on Election Day.

stories.headline: Election Day: control of Congress and dozens of governorships on the line
stories.summary: Voters are heading to the polls nationwide in a midterm election that will determine House and Senate control, with results beginning to trickle in from Kentucky and Indiana at 6 p.m. ET and dragging into the early hours with Alaska's toss-up Senate race.

stories.headline: Cook Political Report's final calls: Democrats now favored for both House and Senate majorities
stories.summary: The nonpartisan Cook Political Report issued its last pre-election ratings finding Democrats favored to win a Senate majority on the strength of the Michigan race, after earlier projecting Democrats could win up to 240 House seats, which would be their largest majority since 2009.

stories.headline: Haley Stevens' surprise endorsement of GOP's Mike Rogers roils Michigan Senate race days before voting
stories.summary: Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens crossed party lines to endorse Republican Mike Rogers over her own party's nominee Abdul El-Sayed, a last-minute jolt to a Senate race that could decide chamber control, escalating a feud that has drawn commentary from Fox News, National Review and Vice President JD Vance.

stories.headline: Supreme Court rejects Trump DOJ's eleventh-hour bid to freeze California ballot counting
stories.summary: Hours before polls opened, the Supreme Court denied the Trump administration's last-ditch appeal seeking to force California to set aside ballots from suspected noncitizen voters, a case that had been fast-tracked in the campaign's final days.

stories.headline: U.S. strikes Iran's Qeshm Island as Trump downplays renewed war risk on Election Day
stories.summary: The U.S. struck Iran's Qeshm Island even as President Trump sought to play down prospects of a return to war with Iran, while separate reporting indicates Trump is weighing further strikes once midterm voting concludes.

stories.headline: Trump DOJ's election-administration fights intensify on voting day
stories.summary: A federal judge ordered the Justice Department to ensure its poll monitors are not law enforcement officers after the NAACP's broader challenge failed, part of a wider pattern of DOJ election lawsuits — including an uphill Alaska Senate ballot appeal and a court order keeping a block on DOJ action over a disputed voter list — that courts have largely rebuffed despite repeated losses.

stories.headline: Senate control could come down to a knife's edge, with a possible 50-50 tie scenario in play
stories.summary: With Senate control uncertain, Fox News examined how past 50-50 splits in 2000 and 2020 could offer a roadmap if Tuesday's results produce another tied chamber, as nail-biter races in Alaska, South Carolina, Georgia and Michigan head toward final counts.

US politics.gaps: NOTUS's recent public output found via search predates the 48-hour window (its most recent 2026-election stories were weeks to months old), so no current NOTUS coverage could be confirmed. Cook Political Report's own site did not surface directly in search; its ratings are reported here only as cited by other outlets (Washington Post, Axios, Washington Examiner, NPR, Fox News).

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage is dominated by Anthropic's blockbuster but risk-laden IPO filing, Apple's mixed Q4 earnings overshadowed by iPhone Duo supply constraints, and a wave of AI-geopolitics stories spanning Nvidia-China restrictions, Chinese AI safety rules, and OpenAI's new ties to U.S. national security. A secondary thread covers AI security incidents (a Google-banned Android TV botnet) and industry self-policing (Anthropic curbing game-cloning in Claude Code).

stories.headline: Anthropic's IPO filing reveals $895 billion compute tab and slowing growth
stories.summary: Anthropic's revised S-1 shows nearly $900 billion in compute and infrastructure commitments against $17 billion in Q3 revenue, with the filing warning that its recent 12x revenue growth rate is unlikely to continue; The Register notes the company's non-cancellable deals with Microsoft, Google, Amazon and Broadcom now total $437 billion.

stories.headline: Apple's earnings overshadowed by iPhone Duo supply crunch and cautious new CEO tone
stories.summary: Apple CEO John Ternus told Reuters the company still can't predict when iPhone Duo supply constraints will ease, even as Apple posted a record iPhone sales quarter and guided to lower gross margins due to "unprecedented" memory costs.

stories.headline: OpenAI hires former Army Secretary Dan Driscoll for national security push
stories.summary: Former U.S. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll, who stepped down after reportedly clashing with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, is joining OpenAI as a senior counselor to expand the company's technology in military and national-security applications.

stories.headline: Google bans Android TV box maker after discovering 1.3 million-device botnet backdoor
stories.summary: Google says an Android manufacturing partner secretly built a backdoor into 1.3 million set-top boxes to run a botnet, and the company says it has now dismantled the operation and cut ties with the maker.

stories.headline: China signals broad new AI safety standards after global security incidents
stories.summary: A senior Chinese economic planning official said Beijing will closely monitor AI's impact on employment as the country moves to set safety standards and ethical guidelines covering the "whole life cycle of AI," according to The Information.

stories.headline: Nvidia pushes cloud customers to scale back China business
stories.summary: Nvidia has told some cloud customers to take on less business from Chinese companies, though The Decoder notes the request is not mandatory.

stories.headline: AI stock selloff deepens ahead of US midterms, hitting chipmakers and metals
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports AMD faces pressure to deliver a strong outlook to avoid Intel's fate amid rising skepticism about AI spending, a theme echoed by a related Bloomberg report on copper and base metals sliding on the renewed tech selloff; WSJ and FT separately frame Tuesday's US midterm elections as a referendum on the AI infrastructure buildout.

stories.headline: Anthropic cracks down on Claude Code game-cloning amid AI copycat boom
stories.summary: Anthropic is blocking its Claude Code coding assistant from recreating existing video games after a wave of AI-built knockoffs, though Ars Technica argues the rule change won't be enough to stem the broader wave of AI-generated game clones across the industry.

Tech & AI.gaps: Could not find outlet-verified recent coverage from Wired, NYT, FT, The Economist, or The Guardian beyond what appeared in the provided feed items, since these outlets block direct web search.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are dominated by a wave of Q3 earnings and megadeal news (NextEra-Dominion, Aramco, Dominion, Exelon), alongside geopolitical energy stories tied to the Iran strikes and a U.S. push to revive Russian gas flows to Europe via Ukraine. Climate-policy coverage centers on new modeling of the U.S. permitting bill's emissions impact and the upcoming COP31 summit in Antalya, while the economics field mourns Nobel laureate William Nordhaus.

stories.headline: NextEra Agrees to More Safeguards for $67 Billion Dominion Deal
stories.summary: NextEra Energy offered Virginia regulators additional customer and financial protections in its latest attempt to win approval for its $67 billion acquisition of Dominion Energy.

stories.headline: Saudi Aramco Profit Surges Despite Pipeline and Refinery Attacks
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's state oil giant posted a profit jump that WSJ attributed to higher crude volumes from steady production plus stronger refined-product and chemical prices, offering relief to the kingdom's finances.

stories.headline: U.S. Pushes to Restore Russian Gas Sales to Europe Via Ukraine
stories.summary: Washington is floating a plan to unlock an energy ceasefire between Moscow and Kyiv by restoring Russian gas sales through Ukraine, though the idea faces pushback in European capitals.

stories.headline: Oil Prices Rebound as U.S. Strikes on Iran Renew Supply Concerns
stories.summary: Oil prices recovered some of the prior session's losses as investors weighed fresh U.S. strikes on Iran against ongoing diplomatic efforts to de-escalate.

stories.headline: New Modeling Finds Permitting Bill Would Likely Cut Emissions
stories.summary: A new Rhodium Group analysis found the bipartisan permitting bill known as BAAJA would likely cut U.S. emissions by 2040, or at worst leave them flat, because transmission gains from the bill outweigh the emissions boost from easier gas pipeline permitting.

stories.headline: Interactive: Who Wants What at the COP31 Climate Change Summit
stories.summary: Carbon Brief previews the upcoming UN climate negotiations in Antalya, Turkey, noting delegates will gather against a backdrop of war and competing national priorities.

stories.headline: William Nordhaus Has Died, Nobelist Influenced Climate Policy
stories.summary: The Yale economist who brought climate change into mainstream economic analysis and won the Nobel Prize has died, NYT reports.

stories.headline: Exelon Eyes $8B in Energy Storage, Partly to Address PJM Supply Crunch
stories.summary: Exelon's CEO Calvin Butler said PJM isn't adding generation fast enough and detailed plans to invest roughly $8 billion in storage and transmission to help close the gap, alongside Dominion reporting a $137 million net income boost from a rate increase.

Energy.gaps: No material from Argus Media could be retrieved this round (search quota exhausted before it could be checked). E&E News, Canary Media and Latitude Media are blocked from fresh web search in this session or returned only older items (no verified stories within the last 24-48 hours), so they are not represented beyond general site context.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage across these outlets centers on Beijing's emergency measures to stabilize a slumping stock market, preparations for a possible Trump-Putin-Xi summit around the Shenzhen APEC meeting, a tightening of Communist Party internal discipline, and a wave of China-linked corporate news from Apple's revenue miss to layoffs at BMW's China venture. Hong Kong's Joshua Wong sentencing and continued buildup of China's amphibious naval fleet also feature prominently, alongside Taiwan's trade and diplomatic maneuvering with Japan and Beijing.

stories.headline: Beijing rolls out stock-support package as market slump deepens
stories.summary: China announced a coordinated package Monday easing share-buyback rules, preparing a third round of a central bank swap facility, and making a lending program for buybacks and stake increases permanent to shore up a declining stock market. The move follows the CSI300's worst month since early 2016, with over 100 billion yuan already applied for under the swap facility.

stories.headline: Trump, Putin and Xi meeting floated ahead of Shenzhen APEC summit
stories.summary: The US, Russia and China are reportedly discussing a possible trilateral meeting between Trump, Putin and Xi, with the US president set to travel to Shenzhen for the APEC summit in two weeks. Xi has said Shenzhen will host the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in November, the third time China has hosted the gathering.

stories.headline: Communist Party tightens surveillance of officials' assets and online activity
stories.summary: A new party document outlines plans to scrutinize officials' assets and online behavior more closely, part of a broader anti-corruption push following the party's fifth plenum. Nikkei Asia separately reported the party is deploying big-data surveillance tools to detect bribery and nepotism among members.

stories.headline: Joshua Wong to be sentenced Thursday in second national security trial
stories.summary: A Hong Kong court has set Thursday to sentence pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong in his second national security case, which could carry a sentence of up to life imprisonment.

stories.headline: Apple's Greater China revenue grows but misses forecasts
stories.summary: Apple reported Greater China revenue of $17.54 billion for its fiscal fourth quarter, up 21% year-on-year but below market expectations of $18.75 billion, underscoring the uneven nature of its China recovery.

stories.headline: BMW's China joint venture cuts about 1,800 jobs amid sales pressure
stories.summary: BMW Brilliance reportedly began layoffs on November 2 affecting multiple job categories, mainly production workers, as the German automaker's China venture grapples with weakening sales.

stories.headline: China doubles down on amphibious warship fleet, raising Taiwan invasion concerns
stories.summary: Beijing is expanding production of Type 071 amphibious transport docks to a second shipyard, with six new vessels under construction that could boost its amphibious fleet by 75% to 14 ships, challenging US assessments that China lacks sufficient lift capacity for a Taiwan assault. Analysts cited in the report say the expansion signals growing urgency in Beijing's push to develop a credible invasion option, though some dispute that lift capacity was ever a major constraint.

stories.headline: Taiwan seeks formal APEC invitation from China amid trade-pact talks with Japan
stories.summary: Taiwan's premier said the government is working to secure a formal invitation from China to the Shenzhen APEC summit after reports that Beijing departed from protocol by emailing rather than formally inviting Taipei, while declining to comment on a possible Taiwan-Japan trade pact that could be finalized by year's end.

China.gaps: Sixth Tone, China Media Project, Yicai Global, CGTN, China Daily, Xinhua, ChinaTalk, Pandaily, Rest of World, and Reuters/AP/NYT (search-blocked) had no distinct China-politics/economy leads beyond what's reflected above in the last 24-48 hours based on available feed items and searches.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Gulf and Middle East outlets are dominated by the fragile US-Iran conflict after fresh American strikes on Qeshm Island, alongside the aftermath of Israel's inconclusive election as opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot tries to build a coalition to replace Netanyahu. Business coverage centers on Saudi Aramco's strong quarterly earnings amid the regional war and major Gulf corporate deal-making, while Gaza violence and regional security incidents round out the agenda.

stories.headline: US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island as drone downed, war fears resurface on US election day
stories.summary: The US carried out what officials called defensive strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island after Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they downed a US drone, reviving fears of a return to full-scale war even as diplomatic efforts continue; a senior Iranian official told Reuters the two sides remain far from a deal and Tehran would respond forcefully to any further strikes.

stories.headline: Israeli opposition bloc scrambles to oust Netanyahu after inconclusive election
stories.summary: Gadi Eisenkot's anti-Netanyahu bloc met to plot a path to government, pledging to begin coalition talks and replace the Knesset speaker, while haredi parties and Liberman's refusal to back a minority government backed by Arab parties could prove decisive.

stories.headline: Israeli forces kill 19 Palestinians in Gaza over three days
stories.summary: The Palestinian Health Ministry said Israeli forces killed 19 Palestinians in Gaza since Saturday, with separate reports of air strikes on a university and police officers killed near Khan Younis.

stories.headline: Saudi Aramco's Q3 profit surges 34.6% as war keeps oil prices elevated
stories.summary: Saudi oil giant Aramco announced a 34.6 percent surge in third-quarter net profit to $36.2 billion as the Middle East war keeps crude prices high even as the kingdom's energy infrastructure comes under regular attack.

stories.headline: Emaar studies buyout of its $15 billion construction arm
stories.summary: Dubai's Emaar Properties is considering plans to take over its listed construction arm in a potential multibillion-dollar deal, according to people familiar with the matter.

stories.headline: 2027 Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia postponed to December after regional attacks
stories.summary: Asian football's governing body postponed the 2027 Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia from January to December citing "exceptional circumstances" in the region, a move that will also ripple through Europe's big leagues and Gulf football schedules.

stories.headline: Saudi wealth fund raises $3 billion loan backed by Italy's export credit agency
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund raised loans equivalent to around $3 billion guaranteed by Italy's Sace insurer and export credit agency, deepening financial ties between Riyadh and Rome.

stories.headline: Syria foils Hezbollah-linked plot to blow up oil refinery
stories.summary: Syrian authorities said they thwarted a plot linked to Hezbollah aimed at blowing up an oil refinery, underscoring persistent cross-border security threats tied to the wider regional conflict.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Could not retrieve recent material from Arabian Business, AGBI, Zawya, Al Arabiya English, or The New Arab beyond what search returned; Reuters, AP, FT, NYT, WSJ, The Economist and BBC coverage is limited to the feed items provided since these outlets block direct search.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage across African and international outlets is dominated by the fallout from Washington's decision to strip South Africa and Rwanda of AGOA trade privileges, alongside South Africa's fragmented municipal election results and a wave of business news around Dangote's refinery IPO and the AFIS banking summit in Luanda. Security and political stories also feature heavily, including renewed Ethiopia-Tigray fighting, Uganda's arrest of a former deputy army chief, and the ICC's clash with the Trump administration over sanctions.

stories.headline: US kicks South Africa, Rwanda out of AGOA
stories.summary: Washington has formally removed South Africa and Rwanda from the African Growth and Opportunity Act after months of diplomatic tension, a long-anticipated move with major implications for trade access and jobs in both countries.

stories.headline: South Africa: Can fragmented parties find common ground after municipal elections?
stories.summary: A record number of parties contested South Africa's municipal elections, leaving most major cities facing fragmented results and difficult coalition negotiations to form governing majorities.

stories.headline: Dangote refinery's $1.6 billion IPO draws nearly triple demand
stories.summary: Nigerian investors placed roughly $4.78 billion in orders for Dangote's oversubscribed refinery listing ahead of its planned November debut, underscoring strong domestic appetite for the country's biggest-ever IPO.

stories.headline: AFIS 2026: In Angola, African finance faces the challenge of funding the real economy
stories.summary: More than 1,250 participants gathered in Luanda for the sixth Africa Financial Summit, debating how to turn individual financial success stories into broader, productive investment across the continent.

stories.headline: Ethiopia's Tigray rebels claim to have inflicted heavy losses on army
stories.summary: Tigrayan forces say they killed 500 soldiers and wounded 800 more in a counteroffensive near Aksum, as fighting between Addis Ababa and the Tigray region reignites.

stories.headline: ICC president hits back at Trump administration penalties
stories.summary: The International Criminal Court's president accused the Trump administration of trying to obstruct international justice through sanctions on the tribunal and vowed the effort would fail.

stories.headline: Burkina Faso: Russian security firms battle for control of a gold mine
stories.summary: A rivalry between Russian security contractors has erupted over control of security at Nordgold's Bissa mine in Burkina Faso, with internal letters showing the sidelined RSB-Group fighting to retain its position.

stories.headline: Gemcorp joins Madagascar to raise $5bn for energy, mining
stories.summary: Madagascar is partnering with asset manager Gemcorp Capital Management in an effort to raise as much as $5 billion to fund energy, infrastructure and mining projects on the island.

Africa.gaps: Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ were not in the provided feed items and are blocked from web search, so no recent coverage from them could be confirmed. The Continent's site returned only older PDF archive issues rather than current-week content.

Media.overview: Coverage clusters around AI’s disruption of publishing — new opt-out tools from AI giants, fresh publisher lawsuits, and simmering anger at Meta’s scraping terms — alongside wall-to-wall industry prep for U.S. midterm election night. Entertainment-business outlets are also absorbing a wave of Q3 earnings (Disney layoffs, Versant, Cinemark) and insider media-newsletter scoops from Status and Puck.

stories.headline: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Microsoft to simplify publisher opt-outs from AI scraping
stories.summary: The four AI giants announced a joint mechanism so publishers no longer have to block each company's web crawlers individually, a shift that could reshape how news sites control AI access to their content.

stories.headline: Newsrooms brace for an unpredictable U.S. midterm election night
stories.summary: Television networks are flooding the airwaves with midterm coverage, including extended NBC programming and a continuous Steve Kornacki big-board livestream, as newsrooms across the industry gear up for results night.

stories.headline: Status scoop: Fox News ratings plunge ahead of midterms, pressuring Murdochs
stories.summary: Independent newsletter Status reports that sliding Fox News ratings and Trump's fading political fortunes are forcing a reckoning inside the Murdoch family's media empire, a story Status says it first broke last week.

stories.headline: Disney prepares thousands more layoffs in push for 20% cost cuts
stories.summary: Disney is laying groundwork for a new, larger round of job cuts across its TV and film divisions just a week after theme parks eliminated at least 100 positions, as the company pushes for deep cost savings.

stories.headline: Versant's Q3 revenue slips despite digital and ratings gains
stories.summary: The MS NOW and CNBC parent company beat Wall Street estimates with $1.59 billion in quarterly revenue, even as traditional media advertising and distribution lines continued to soften.

stories.headline: Publishers furious over Meta's AI scraping terms, but can't afford to quit the platform
stories.summary: Publishers are pushing back against changed Meta terms allowing AI scraping of their content, but most feel they lack real leverage because they still depend on Facebook for traffic.

stories.headline: AI-publisher legal war escalates: new lawsuits against Brave and Anthropic
stories.summary: Press Gazette's running tracker shows U.S. newspapers suing Brave Software and Canadian publishers suing Anthropic, the latest moves in a widening global legal battle between news publishers and AI firms.

stories.headline: Puck: Kalshi courts credibility by sponsoring news organizations
stories.summary: Puck's Dylan Byers reports that prediction market Kalshi is striking sponsorship deals with outlets like CNN and CBS News to position itself as a journalistic gauge of public sentiment rather than a sports-betting platform, even though most of its bets are on sports.

Media.gaps: FT had no media-industry items in the feed and was not searchable directly; WSJ, The Guardian and NYT coverage is limited to the single feed items provided since those outlets block search.
